unit.title: Argumentative Connectors
unit.subtitle: Formal connectors that signal contrast, concession, and consequence

grammar.title: Steer an argument like a native writer
grammar.intro: At C1, what separates you from an intermediate speaker is how you connect ideas in formal, written, or argued Spanish. Words like no obstante (nevertheless), por consiguiente (therefore), and ahora bien (that said) each signal a precise logical relation and belong to an elevated register. One of them, de ahí que, even forces the subjunctive. Master these and your prose reads as native argumentation, not translation.

sections.heading: Contrast: no obstante, sin embargo, en cambio, por el contrario
sections.body: These flag that what follows runs against the previous idea. Sin embargo and no obstante are near-synonyms (nevertheless), the second being more formal. En cambio contrasts two subjects (by contrast), while por el contrario corrects with the opposite (on the contrary). Note the punctuation: sentence-initial they take a comma; mid-sentence they sit between commas.
conj: by contrast / on the other hand

ex.es: El plan es ambicioso; no obstante, carece de financiación.
ex.en: The plan is ambitious; nevertheless, it lacks funding.

ex.es: Él prefiere la cautela; ella, por el contrario, arriesga.
ex.en: He prefers caution; she, on the contrary, takes risks.

sections.heading: Consequence: por (lo) tanto, por consiguiente, por ende, así pues
sections.body: These draw a conclusion from what precedes (therefore, consequently). Por lo tanto is the everyday-formal choice; por consiguiente and por ende are markedly literary; así pues wraps up an argument (thus, so then). They introduce a result the reader should accept as following logically.

ex.es: Los datos son concluyentes; por consiguiente, revisaremos la política.
ex.en: The data are conclusive; consequently, we will revise the policy.

ex.es: No hubo consenso; así pues, se aplazó la votación.
ex.en: There was no consensus; thus, the vote was postponed.

sections.heading: de ahí que + subjunctive
sections.body: De ahí que means 'which is why / hence' and, crucially, it requires the subjunctive because it presents the consequence as a derived conclusion rather than a plain fact. Say de ahí que sea, not de ahí que es. It is a hallmark of polished C1 writing.

ex.es: El mercado es volátil; de ahí que los inversores desconfíen.
ex.en: The market is volatile; which is why investors are wary.

ex.es: Nunca documentó el proceso; de ahí que nadie lo entienda.
ex.en: He never documented the process; hence nobody understands it.

sections.heading: Concession & pivot: ahora bien, aun así
sections.body: Ahora bien introduces a qualifying pivot ('that said / now then') — you accept the prior point but add a caveat. Aun así means 'even so / and yet', conceding an obstacle and pressing on anyway. Do not confuse aun así (even so) with aún (still, with accent).

ex.es: La propuesta es sólida. Ahora bien, conviene matizar sus costes.
ex.en: The proposal is sound. That said, its costs should be qualified.

ex.es: Sabía que fracasaría; aun así, lo intentó.
ex.en: He knew he would fail; even so, he tried.

takeaways: Contrast: no obstante / sin embargo (nevertheless), en cambio (by contrast), por el contrario (on the contrary).
Consequence: por lo tanto, por consiguiente, por ende, así pues (therefore / thus).
de ahí que ALWAYS takes the subjunctive: de ahí que sea, not 'de ahí que es'.
ahora bien = qualifying pivot; aun así = 'even so' (no accent on aun).

mistakes.w: El clima cambia, de ahí que hace más calor.
mistakes.r: El clima cambia, de ahí que haga más calor.
mistakes.why: 'De ahí que' triggers the subjunctive: haga, not the indicative hace.

mistakes.w: Es caro. Sin embargo caro, lo compró.
mistakes.r: Es caro. Aun así, lo compró.
mistakes.why: For 'even so' after conceding an obstacle, use 'aun así', not a doubled 'sin embargo'.

mistakes.w: Trabajó mucho, por lo tanto que aprobó.
mistakes.r: Trabajó mucho; por lo tanto, aprobó.
mistakes.why: 'Por lo tanto' is not followed by 'que'; it introduces the clause directly after a comma.

exercises.prompt: La teoría es elegante; ___, no resiste la prueba empírica.
exercises.prompt_en: The theory is elegant; nevertheless, it does not withstand empirical testing.
exercises.no: The two clauses clash, so you need a contrast marker: 'no obstante' (nevertheless).

exercises.prompt: El proceso nunca se documentó; de ahí que nadie lo ___.
exercises.prompt_en: The process was never documented; which is why nobody understands it.
exercises.no: 'De ahí que' forces the subjunctive: 'entienda', not the indicative 'entiende'.

exercises.prompt: Build: "The evidence is conclusive; consequently, we will revise the policy."
exercises.no: For a conclusion you draw from the evidence, use 'por consiguiente' (consequently), not the contrast marker 'sin embargo'.

exercises.prompt: La propuesta es sólida. ___, conviene matizar sus costes.
exercises.prompt_en: The proposal is sound. That said, its costs should be qualified.
exercises.hint: A two-word pivot meaning 'that said / now then'.
exercises.no: The qualifying pivot 'that said' is 'ahora bien'.

exercises.prompt: Match each connector to the logical relation it signals.
exercises.ok: ¡Excelente! Dominas la lógica de cada conector.

exercises.tts: No obstante, cabe señalar una excepción.
accepted: no obstante cabe senalar una excepcion
exercises.translation: Nevertheless, an exception should be noted.
exercises.no: It was: “No obstante, cabe señalar una excepción.” (Nevertheless, an exception should be noted.)

exercises.scenario: Defending a thesis before a committee 🎓

lines.speaker: Tribunal
lines.es: Su corpus es reducido. ¿No invalida eso sus conclusiones?
lines.en: Your corpus is small. Doesn't that invalidate your conclusions?

options.text: Es limitado; aun así, los patrones son estadísticamente significativos.
Sí, por lo tanto no sirve para nada, la verdad.
De ahí que es un corpus pequeño, no pasa nada.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! 'Aun así' concede el límite y sigue argumentando.
exercises.no: Concede the objection yet press on with 'aun así' (even so); option c misuses 'de ahí que' with the indicative.

exercises.say: El argumento es válido; por ende, lo acepto.
exercises.en: The argument is valid; hence, I accept it.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “El argumento es válido; por ende, lo acepto.”
